propositions: Line-start marker strings (VOTER_ERROR, MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR, etc.) are emitted twice — once via logger.error/warning and once via print to stderr — causing journald to ingest duplicate lines with identical timestamps

The probe at observability.sh anchors on the marker token (^VOTER_ERROR \{) and counts both the logger-streamed stdout copy and the stderr print, doubling the metric rebar/host:voter_errors and misaligning downstream alarms

Fix: keep only the unconditional print(line, file=sys.stderr) as the single line-start marker emission (the failsafe path), and change logger calls to emit the structured record body without the token prefix so logged copies are not probe-countable

Four confirmed sibling sites exhibit the same dual-emission construct: MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR (live-doubling), and three latent (RECONCILE_DEGRADED, ARTIFACT_EMIT_ERROR, LLM_TOKEN_USAGE), all fixed in scope with identical change
Structural class-guard test prevents future markers from reintroducing the dual line-start emission pattern by scanning for token-prefixed strings passed to logger calls
